Diagnosis:
The test "testEscapedQuote_LANG_477" fails due to an OutOfMemoryError when creating an ExtendedMessageFormat object with a pattern containing single quotes and a custom format registry. The specific pattern used is `it''s a {0,lower} 'test'!`.

The constructor ExtendedMessageFormat(String pattern, Map registry) delegates to ExtendedMessageFormat(String pattern, Locale locale, Map registry) which initializes the object and calls applyPattern(pattern).

In ExtendedMessageFormat.applyPattern(String), when a custom registry is present, it manually parses the pattern. It iterates over the pattern characters and processes quoted strings and format elements accordingly. When it encounters a single quote character (QUOTE), it calls appendQuotedString(pattern, pos, stripCustom, true).

The appendQuotedString method handles quoted strings in the pattern, supporting escaping of quotes by doubling them. It iterates over the characters starting at the position of the quote and appends the quoted content, properly handling doubled quotes as escaped quotes. If it reaches the end without closing the quote, it throws an IllegalArgumentException for unterminated quote.

The test pattern contains a doubled single quote `''` at "it''s" which is correctly interpreted as an escaped single quote. It also contains a quoted string `'test'` later in the pattern.

The likely cause of the OutOfMemoryError is an infinite loop or runaway parsing in appendQuotedString or in the pattern parsing loop of applyPattern. This is consistent with the report describing an OutOfMemoryError for patterns with single quotes and a custom registry.

Specifically, in appendQuotedString, the logic to advance the ParsePosition pos and to handle quotes might have an issue if the escapingOn flag and the detection of escaped quotes don't handle the transition correctly causing pos not to advance properly or the loop to never end.

In summary, the OutOfMemoryError arises due to faulty handling of single quotes in ExtendedMessageFormat.applyPattern and appendQuotedString when a custom format registry is used, causing an infinite parsing loop or excessive memory usage while trying to parse the pattern with escaped quotes and quoted literals.

The test triggers this because it uses a pattern with escaped quotes and quoted literals and a custom registry, which causes applyPattern to take the branch with parsing logic that malfunctions on this input.

The root cause is a bug in the appendQuotedString method's handling of single quotes with escaping enabled inside ExtendedMessageFormat when a custom format registry is present.

Recent bug reports are unrelated to this specific logic.

Next, we should pinpoint exact lines inside appendQuotedString and applyPattern that cause the loop or incorrect position advancement.
ExtendedMessageFormat.applyPattern(String)
ExtendedMessageFormat.appendQuotedString(String, ParsePosition, StringBuffer, boolean)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
